facts.statement: General housing allowance can be paid to households consisting of a single person or several persons.
facts.quote: General housing allowance can be paid to households consisting of a single person or several persons.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.quote: Housing allowance is granted to the household as a unit, so the amount of housing allowance will depend on the total income and assets of the entire household.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: General housing allowance is available for rental, right-of-occupancy and part-ownership housing.
facts.quote: General housing allowance is available for rental, right-of-occupancy and part-ownership housing.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: A household can get housing allowance only if its income does not exceed the income limit for its municipality.
facts.quote: You can get housing allowance if your income does not exceed the income limit for your municipality.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: Only part of the housing costs are taken into account when calculating the housing allowance.
facts.quote: Only part of your housing costs are taken into account when calculating your housing allowance.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.quote: Use our calculator to check how much housing allowance you might get. The result is an estimate.

facts.statement: The citizen can apply for housing allowance either on a form or in the OmaKela e-service.
facts.quote: You can apply for housing allowance either on a form or in the OmaKela e-service.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: Maximum limits for recognised housing costs (maximum housing costs) are defined and vary by municipality.
facts.quote: Maximum limits have been defined for recognised housing costs. They vary by municipality, and they are also known as maximum housing costs.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: The housing allowance cannot exceed the municipality-specific maximum limit for recognised housing costs.
facts.quote: The amount of housing allowance you can get cannot exceed the municipality-specific maximum limit for recognised housing costs.
facts.locator: H2: Can you get general housing allowance?

facts.statement: As a rule, students cannot get general housing allowance; most students can get the housing supplement for students instead.
facts.quote: If you study, you cannot, as a rule, get general housing allowance. The majority of students can get the housing supplement for students to help with their housing costs.
facts.locator: H3: Are you a student?

facts.statement: A student can qualify for general housing allowance instead of the student housing supplement if they live with their own child or their partner's child.
facts.quote:
However, you can qualify for general housing allowance instead of the student housing supplement for example in the following situations:
You live with your own child or your partner’s child.
facts.locator: H3: Are you a student?

facts.statement: A student can qualify for general housing allowance if during studies they are paid another benefit that is not student financial aid, such as unemployment benefits, rehabilitation allowance or sickness allowance.
facts.quote: You are paid some other benefit during your studies that is not student financial aid, such as unemployment benefits, rehabilitation allowance or sickness allowance.
facts.locator: H3: Are you a student?

facts.statement: A student can qualify for general housing allowance if they have suspended their studies or used up all available months of student financial aid.
facts.quote: You have suspended your studies or used up all months of student financial aid available to you.
facts.locator: H3: Are you a student?

facts.statement: A student can qualify for general housing allowance if Kela has stopped payment of their student financial aid due to insufficient study progress.
facts.quote: You have not made enough progress during your studies and we have stopped the payment of your student financial aid as a result
facts.locator: H3: Are you a student?

facts.statement: Pensioners who live permanently in Finland, have a low income and receive a qualifying pension can get the housing allowance for pensioners.
facts.quote: You can get housing allowance for pensioners if you are living permanently in Finland, you have a low income and you receive a pension which entitles you to the housing allowance for pensioners.
facts.locator: H3: Are you a pensioner?

facts.statement: A person who has moved to Finland from another country may have the right to general housing allowance if they live in Finland permanently.
facts.quote: You may have the right to general housing allowance (yleinen asumistuki) if you have moved to Finland from another country and you live in Finland permanently.
facts.locator: H3: Have you moved to Finland from another country?

facts.statement: A person is usually considered to live in Finland permanently after living in Finland for one year.
facts.quote: You will usually be considered to be living in Finland permanently after you have lived in Finland for one year.
facts.locator: H3: Have you moved to Finland from another country?

facts.statement: Only persons who live in Finland can belong to the same household for general housing allowance.
facts.quote: General housing allowance is paid to a household. Only persons who live in Finland can belong to the same household.
facts.locator: H3: Have you moved to Finland from another country?

facts.statement: A citizen of an EU or EEA country or Switzerland who moved to Finland to work may have the right to general housing allowance.
facts.quote: You may have the right to general housing allowance if you have moved to Finland to work and you are the citizen of an EU or EEA country or Switzerland.
facts.locator: H4: Did you come to Finland to work?

facts.statement: A person who has fled the war in Ukraine may have the right to general housing allowance if they live in Finland permanently.
facts.quote: You may have the right to general housing allowance if you have fled the war in Ukraine and you live in Finland permanently.
facts.locator: H4: Have you fled the war in Ukraine?

facts.statement: A household typically includes the persons sharing a home on a permanent basis, and a person can only be a member of one household at a time.
facts.quote: A household typically includes the persons sharing a home on a permanent basis. You can only be a member of one household at a time.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: One member of the household applies for housing allowance on behalf of the entire household.
facts.quote: One member of the household applies for housing allowance on behalf of the entire household.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Married persons or persons in a relationship who share a home belong to the same household regardless of whether they have joint or separate rental agreements.
facts.quote: Persons who are married or in a relationship and are sharing a home belong to the same household regardless of whether they have a joint rental agreement or separate rental agreements.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A spouse or partner entitled to the housing supplement for students is not part of the household, so their income and assets do not affect the general housing allowance.
facts.quote: A spouse or partner who is entitled to the housing supplement for students is not considered part of the household. Their income or assets therefore do not affect the amount of the general housing allowance.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Married couples living at different addresses belong to the same household if they live apart because of e.g. work, studies, or military or non-military service in another municipality.
facts.quote: Married couples living at different addresses also belong to the same household if the reason that they live apart is, for example, work, studies, or military or non-military service in another municipality.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Married spouses are in different households if they live apart because their relationship has ended.
facts.quote: Married spouses are considered to be part of different households if they live apart because their relationship has ended.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Roommates with a joint rental agreement, or who are jointly responsible for paying rent under the agreement or its appendix, belong to the same household.
facts.quote:
Roommates can be part of the same household or two different households.
roommates with a joint rental agreement
roommates who under the rental agreement (or an appendix to the agreement) are jointly responsible for paying rent.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Roommates belonging to the same household must authorise one household member to apply for housing allowance for the whole household.
facts.quote: Roommates belonging to the same household must authorise one member of their household to apply for housing allowance for the whole household.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Authorisation of one roommate household member is given with the form 'Power of attorney to represent a communal household' AT5e.
facts.quote: Use the form ‘Power of attorney to represent a communal household’ AT5e (PDF) to authorise one household member.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: If housing allowance is granted to a roommate household, it is paid to the authorised person.
facts.quote: If housing allowance is granted to the household, it is paid to the authorised person.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Roommates with separate rental agreements or who sublet an apartment can be in different households, provided they are not jointly responsible for paying rent for the entire dwelling under the rental agreement or its appendix.
facts.quote:
roommates with separate rental agreements
roommates who are subletting an apartment
Further, in order to be considered to be part of different households, roommates may not be jointly responsible for paying rent for the entire dwelling
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A married couple, cohabiting couple or close relatives (parents, children, grandparents) living at the same address are in the same household regardless of their rental agreement terms.
facts.quote: A married couple, a cohabiting couple or close relatives are part of the same household if they live at the same address, regardless of the terms of their rental agreement. Close relatives means parents, children and grandparents.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Siblings sharing a home are in different households if they have separate rental agreements or a sublease agreement.
facts.quote: Siblings sharing a home are part of different households if they have separate rental agreements or a sublease agreement.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A child under 18 living independently with no income is usually considered part of their parents' household.
facts.quote: A child under the age of 18 who is living independently and who has no income is usually considered to be part of their parents’ household.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Adult children (18 or older) living independently are not part of their parents' household, while adult children living with their parents are.
facts.quote:
Adult children (18 or older) who live independently are not part of their parents’ household.
Adult children who live with their parents belong to their parents’ household.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A person temporarily living elsewhere due to work, military or non-military service or similar reasons remains part of the household of their permanent residence.
facts.quote: You are part of the same household as the persons living in your permanent residence even if you live elsewhere temporarily on account of work, military or non-military service, or other similar reasons.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Living elsewhere is usually considered temporary if it lasts less than about a year.
facts.quote: Living elsewhere is usually considered to be temporary if it lasts less than about a year.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A person who has moved to Finland can be part of a household if Kela considers the person to be permanently resident in Finland.
facts.quote: A person who has moved to Finland can be considered part of a household if Kela considers the person to be permanently resident in Finland.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Students who come to Finland cannot belong to a household or get housing allowance.
facts.quote: Students who come to Finland cannot belong to a household or get housing allowance.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: Subtenants belong to a different household than the main tenant or owner, except a subtenant who is the spouse or close relative of the main tenant or owner.
facts.quote:
Subtenants are considered to belong to a different household than the main tenant or owner, with a few exceptions.
A subtenant who is the spouse or close relative of the main tenant or owner is part of the same household.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: A housing allowance recipient must notify Kela if they take in a subtenant.
facts.quote: Notify Kela if you get housing allowance and take in a subtenant.
facts.locator: H3: Who belongs to a household?

facts.statement: If the calculated housing allowance is less than EUR 15 per month, it is not paid out.
facts.quote: If your housing allowance is less than EUR 15 per month, it is not paid out.
facts.locator: H2: How much general housing allowance can you get?

facts.statement: The amount of housing allowance is affected by the number of adults and children in the household, income and assets, eligible housing costs, the municipal maximum housing costs, and the basic deductible.
facts.quote:
The amount of the housing allowance is affected by
the number of adults and children in the household
income and assets
housing costs for which you can get housing allowance
the maximum limits for housing costs defined for each municipality (maximum housing costs)
the basic deductible.
facts.locator: H2: How much general housing allowance can you get?

facts.statement: Kela pays the housing allowance into the recipient's bank account or the landlord's account on the first banking day of the month.
facts.quote: Kela pays the housing allowance into your bank account or your landlord’s account on the first banking day of the month.

facts.statement: If banks are closed on the scheduled payment date, the housing allowance is paid on the next banking day.
facts.quote: If the banks are closed on the scheduled payment date, the housing allowance will be paid on the next banking day.

facts.statement: The housing allowance is tax-free income.
facts.quote: The housing allowance is tax-free income.

facts.statement: Retroactively granted housing allowance generally appears in the bank account within two banking days of payment.
facts.quote: If you get housing allowance retroactively, the allowance will generally appear in your bank account within two banking days of payment.
facts.locator: H3: Payment of the housing allowance

facts.statement: Housing allowance is available retroactively for one month.
facts.quote: Housing allowance is available retroactively for one month.

facts.quote: If you live alone, let us know if you are away from your home for more than 3 months.
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: The right to housing allowance ends if the person is away from home for 3 months or more.
facts.quote: Your right to housing allowance ends if you are away from your home for 3 months or more.
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: A recipient who no longer needs housing allowance notifies Kela that they want it stopped.
facts.quote: If you no longer need housing allowance, let us know that you want your housing allowance stopped.
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: Termination can be requested via a notification in OmaKela (under Ilmoita muutoksista) or a message in OmaKela (under Lähetä ja lue viestejä).
facts.quote: Submit a notification in OmaKela e-service (under Ilmoita muutoksista) or send a message in OmaKela (under Lähetä ja lue viestejä).
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: OmaKela is only available in Finnish and Swedish.
facts.quote: OmaKela is only available in Finnish and Swedish.
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: If the citizen cannot use OmaKela, they fill in form AT 6e 'General housing allowance - Termination of housing allowance' to stop the allowance.
facts.quote: If you cannot use OmaKela, fill in the form ‘General housing allowance - Termination of housing allowance’ AT 6e (PDF).
facts.locator: H3: Report the following changes

facts.statement: Kela reviews the housing allowance at least every 12 months even if household circumstances do not change.
facts.quote: Kela will review your housing allowance at least every 12 months even if your household’s circumstances do not change.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: The date of the next annual review is shown in the OmaKela e-service.
facts.quote: You can see the date for your next annual review in OmaKela e-service.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: Kela sends instructions about the annual review about two months before the scheduled review.
facts.quote: We will send you instructions about the annual review of your housing allowance about two months before the review is scheduled to take place.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: The annual review instructions are delivered as a message in OmaKela.
facts.quote: You will receive the message in OmaKela.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: Information for the annual review is submitted on the application for general housing allowance.
facts.quote: Send us the information needed for the annual review on the application for general housing allowance.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: The annual review application can be filled in in OmaKela, or sent to Kela by post if OmaKela cannot be used.
facts.quote: You can fill in the application in OmaKela e-service (available in Finnish and Swedish). If you cannot use OmaKela, send your application to Kela by post.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: If the application is not submitted in time for the annual review, Kela stops payment of the housing allowance.
facts.quote: If you do not submit the application in time for the review, we will have to stop the payment of your housing allowance.
facts.locator: H2: Annual review

facts.statement: Questions can be addressed to Kela's customer service by phone.
facts.quote: Call Kela’s customer service.
facts.locator: H2: Do you still have questions?

facts.statement: A new online application form allows applying for general social security benefit and general housing allowance at the same time.
facts.quote: Kela has introduced a new online application form that you can use to apply for general social security benefit and general housing allowance at the same time.
facts.locator: H3: New application form introduced for general social security benefit and general housing allowance

facts.statement: The same new online form can be used to report changes affecting general social security benefit and general housing allowance.
facts.quote: You can also use the same form to report any changes that affect these benefits to Kela.
facts.locator: H3: New application form introduced for general social security benefit and general housing allowance
